meta.title: The Lord Is My Shepherd: Jesus Is My Good Shepherd
meta.verseText: The grass withers and the flowers fall, but the word of our God endures forever.
meta.theme: God leads us in every season, caring for us like a good shepherd caring for his sheep.

questions.text: Who wrote Psalm 23?
questions.hint: He was a king who once took care of sheep himself.
questions.explanation: King David wrote Psalm 23, along with many other Psalms in the Bible.

questions.text: Psalm 23 begins, 'The Lord is my ______.'
questions.hint: It's someone who cares for sheep.
questions.explanation: Psalm 23:1 says, 'The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.' God cares for us like a shepherd cares for sheep.

questions.text: Who is called our Good Shepherd in this lesson?
questions.hint: He loves us and takes care of us every day.
questions.explanation: Jesus is our Good Shepherd. He takes care of us just like a shepherd takes care of his sheep.

questions.text: What does a shepherd do for his sheep?
questions.hint: Think about keeping the sheep safe.
questions.explanation: A shepherd protects and cares for his sheep, just like God protects and cares for us.

questions.text: True or False: God leaves us when we are scared.
questions.hint: Remember, God is always with us.
questions.explanation: This is False. God never leaves us. Even in the darkest valley, He is always with us.

questions.text: In Psalm 23, God 'makes me lie down in green ______.'
questions.hint: It's a grassy place where sheep can rest and eat.
questions.explanation: Psalm 23:2 says God 'makes me lie down in green pastures.' This shows God gives us rest and peace.

questions.text: According to Psalm 23, God 'leads me beside still ______.'
questions.hint: It's calm and peaceful, something you can drink.
questions.explanation: Psalm 23:2 says God 'leads me beside still waters,' showing that God gives us peace and rest.

questions.text: What does it mean that 'the Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want'?
options: God gives us what we need
questions.hint: It's about God providing for us.
questions.explanation: 'I shall not want' means God provides what we need. Our Shepherd takes care of us.

questions.text: Which of these is something God provides for us?
questions.hint: Think of the good things you already have.
questions.explanation: God provides many things like food, family, friends, and a home. He gives us what we need.

questions.text: Psalm 23 says, 'Even though I walk through the darkest valley, I will fear no ______.'
questions.hint: It means we don't have to be afraid of bad things.
questions.explanation: Psalm 23:4 says, 'I will fear no evil, for You are with me.' We don't have to be afraid because God is with us.

questions.text: Why don't we have to be afraid in the 'darkest valley'?
questions.hint: Who is always beside us?
questions.explanation: We don't have to fear because God is with us everywhere, even in scary or hard times.

questions.text: What does Psalm 23 mean when it says God 'restores my soul'?
options: God helps us when we're tired or sad
questions.hint: Think about feeling better after being sad or tired.
questions.explanation: 'He restores my soul' means God helps us when we are tired, sad, or make mistakes. He makes us feel new again.

questions.text: Psalm 23 says God 'leads me in paths of ______.'
questions.hint: It's a big word that means the right way to go.
questions.explanation: Psalm 23:3 says God 'leads me in paths of righteousness.' God always shows us the right way to go.

questions.text: True or False: David wrote Psalm 23 during one of the scariest, hardest times of his life.
questions.hint: David trusted God even in hard times.
questions.explanation: This is True. David wrote Psalm 23 during a hard time in his life, yet he still put his trust completely in God.

questions.text: What is this week's BIG IDEA?
options: God leads us in every season
questions.hint: It's about God being with us all year long.
questions.explanation: The BIG IDEA is 'God leads us in every season.' No matter how easy or hard life is, God is always there.

questions.text: The memory verse says, 'The grass withers and the flowers fall, but the word of our God ______ forever.'
questions.hint: It means God's word lasts and stays forever.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:8 says God's word 'endures forever.' Everything else changes, but God's word never fails.

questions.text: What book of the Bible is the memory verse from?
questions.hint: It's an Old Testament prophet's book, chapter 40.
questions.explanation: The memory verse is Isaiah 40:8. It reminds us that God's word lasts forever.

questions.text: True or False: God takes care of us only on sunny, happy days.
questions.hint: Think about the BIG IDEA and 'every season.'
questions.explanation: This is False. God leads us in every season, including hard and dark days, not just happy ones.

questions.text: When you feel scared at night, what can you remember from Psalm 23?
questions.hint: God is with us everywhere.
questions.explanation: When we are scared, we can remember God is always with us, so we do not have to fear.

questions.text: If a friend at school is feeling sad, how can you be like the Good Shepherd's helper?
options: Be kind and care for them
questions.hint: A shepherd cares for others.
questions.explanation: We can show God's love by being kind and caring for others, just like a shepherd cares for the sheep.

questions.text: What is a good way to trust God when something feels hard?
options: Pray and remember God is with me
questions.hint: David prayed and trusted God in hard times.
questions.explanation: We can pray and remember that God is with us, just like David trusted God during hard times.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: 'Surely goodness and ______ will follow me all the days of my life.'
questions.hint: God blesses us with this every day.
questions.explanation: Psalm 23:6 says, 'Surely goodness and love will follow me all the days of my life.' God blesses us with His love every day.

questions.text: In Psalm 23, God 'prepares a ______ before me.'
questions.hint: It's where you might eat a meal.
questions.explanation: Psalm 23:5 says, 'You prepare a table before me.' This shows how God provides and blesses us.

questions.text: What does the shepherd in Jesus' story do when one sheep gets lost (Luke 15)?
options: Goes to find the lost one
questions.hint: The shepherd searches until he finds it.
questions.explanation: In Luke 15:1-7, the shepherd leaves the flock to search for the one lost sheep until he finds it. God cares about every single one of us.

questions.text: In the story of the lost sheep, how does the shepherd feel when he finds it?
questions.hint: He celebrates!
questions.explanation: In Luke 15, the shepherd is filled with joy and celebrates when he finds the lost sheep. Heaven rejoices over each person who comes to God.

questions.text: True or False: God only cares about big groups of people, not about you as one person.
questions.hint: Remember the shepherd who looked for ONE lost sheep.
questions.explanation: This is False. The story of the lost sheep shows God cares about every single person, even just one.

questions.text: Why can we have peace even when the days get darker in fall?
options: Because God stays near us in every season
questions.hint: Think of the BIG IDEA.
questions.explanation: We can have peace because God stays near us in every season and leads us, no matter what.

questions.text: What is one way you can thank God this week for being your Shepherd?
questions.hint: We talk to God through this.
questions.explanation: We can say a prayer of thanks to God for being our Good Shepherd who loves and cares for us.

questions.text: The lesson's Sticky Point is: 'Jesus is my Good Shepherd, and He always ______ me.'
questions.hint: It's what a shepherd does for sheep.
questions.explanation: The Sticky Point is 'Jesus is my Good Shepherd, and He always takes care of me.'

questions.text: How can you help someone who feels 'lost' or left out, like the lost sheep?
options: Include them and be their friend
questions.hint: Do what the shepherd did — go after the one.
questions.explanation: We can include others and be a good friend, showing the same care the shepherd showed the lost sheep.

questions.text: True or False: Because God's word 'endures forever,' we can always trust what the Bible says.
questions.hint: Think about the memory verse, Isaiah 40:8.
questions.explanation: This is True. Since God's word endures forever, we can always trust and rely on the Bible.

questions.text: What did David do instead of being afraid during his hard time?
options: He put his trust in God
questions.hint: That's why he could write such a peaceful Psalm.
questions.explanation: During his hard time, David put his trust completely in God, which is why he could write Psalm 23.

questions.text: When you make a mistake, what does the Good Shepherd help you do?
options: Find the right way to go
questions.hint: Psalm 23 says He leads us in paths of righteousness.
questions.explanation: God helps us when we make mistakes and always shows us the right way to go, leading us in paths of righteousness.

story.summary: During one of the scariest, hardest times of his life, King David wrote Psalm 23. Instead of being afraid, David trusted God completely. He described God as a Good Shepherd who gives us everything we need, leads us to rest in green pastures and beside still waters, restores us when we are tired or sad, and guides us on the right path. Even when we walk through the darkest valley, we do not have to be afraid, because God is always with us. Jesus is our Good Shepherd, and just like the shepherd in Luke 15 who searched for one lost sheep, He cares for every single one of us. No matter the season, God leads us, provides for us, and blesses us with His love every day.

scenes.title: The Shepherd Who Provides
scenes.description: King David, writing during a hard time, calls the Lord his Shepherd. 'The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.' God gives us everything we need — food, family, friends, and a home.

scenes.title: Rest and Peace
scenes.description: God makes us lie down in green pastures and leads us beside still waters. He restores our soul and leads us in paths of righteousness, giving us rest, peace, and the right way to go.

scenes.title: Through the Darkest Valley
scenes.description: Even when we walk through the darkest valley, we will fear no evil, because God is with us. Sometimes we feel scared, but God never leaves us — He is with us everywhere, in every season.

scenes.title: The Good Shepherd Finds the Lost
scenes.description: Jesus is our Good Shepherd. Like the shepherd in Luke 15 who searched for one lost sheep and celebrated when he found it, Jesus cares about every single one of us and always takes care of us.

scenes.title: God Leads Us in Every Season
scenes.description: Surely goodness and love will follow us all the days of our life. God's word endures forever, so we can trust Him and thank Him. No matter how easy or hard life is, God leads us in every season.
